main.result_summary: The 2000-12-22 consolidation is committed as `3912fa6` and not pushed, since the runner pushes after its own checks. Lint and sleep-audit were both green before the commit. The first audit run came back red because I had appended the consolidation note to an inbox log while moving it to the archive. I restored that log exactly as it was and put the note in a new file, `memory/archive/inbox/2000-12-22--mail-2.md`; the second run was green. All 116 messages with notes this week are handled: 113 are cited in memory, and 3 are listed in `dataset/drops/sleep-056.tsv` (Lance's phone number twice, and a list of group birthdays). Seven new topic files cover this week's new threads: the WTI simulation and the proposed round-the-clock WTI trading on EnronOnline, Braveheart and the total return swaps, the JCC/Brent hedge ratio, the agricultural trading report for Hickerson, interviews set for late December and January (Iris Mack, Frank Qian, Tony Hamilton), the Wharton Tiger Team trip on 18-19 January, and visitors planned for 2001. About 35 existing files were updated, with older lines moved to `memory/archive/*/2000/*-2000-12-w51.md` so no file grew past its allowed limit. Twelve people reached five messages and now have entity files, among them Nelson Neale, Jennifer Fraser, James A Hughes and Frank Qian; Steve Lessar has only four, so he gets none yet. To meet the compression quota I cut `internal-meetings`, `stinson-gibner` and `zimin-lu`. The indexes and `state.md` are refreshed, and the five oldest ongoing lines are still valid. The inbox had no sleep task, nothing hit an approval gate, and `questions.md` and `todo.md` stay empty. The runner's untracked `dataset/runs/sleep-056.transcript.jsonl` is left out of the commit.
